title: Applicability and Limitations of Quantum Circuit Cutting in Classical State-Vector Simulation
summary: Circuit cutting partitions a large quantum circuit into smaller subcircuits that can be executed independently and recombined by classical post-processing. In classical state-vector simulation with full-state reconstruction, the runtime is governed by a trade-off between reduced subcircuit size and the overheads of exponentially many subcircuits and full-state reconstruction. For equal partitioning, we derive threshold conditions on the number of cuts below which cutting reduces the wall-clock time.
